articles.title: Sodium Batteries Hit a Tesla-Level Milestone — But There's a Chilly Problem
articles.summary: Chinese company Hina's sodium-ion battery matched Tesla's manufacturing quality in a new study. It's a big step toward cheaper EVs, but it struggles to charge in the cold. Researchers found unexpected copper in the cathode, raising new questions.

articles.title: As Lakes Go Dark, a Fish Shake-Up: Trout Out, Pike In
articles.summary: Freshwater browning is reshaping fish communities across 871 North American and European lakes. Trout, bass, and perch are declining as water darkens, while walleye and pike thrive thanks to specialized senses. The study offers practical tips for anglers.

articles.title: Your Brain's 'Railway Tracks' Could Derail Alzheimer's, Scientists Say
articles.summary: Baylor researchers found that tubulin, the building block of microtubules, prevents Tau and alpha-synuclein from forming toxic clumps linked to Alzheimer's and Parkinson's. The study suggests boosting tubulin could be a new therapeutic strategy.
